scenario: Mid-career employee with a workplace pension they don't understand and a stale personal pension from a previous job.
transcript: I'm 41, I work in marketing, salary about £55k. I've got my current workplace pension where my employer matches up to 5%, and I'm pretty sure there's a pot somewhere from a job I had between 2014 and 2018 — Aviva maybe? I've never looked at either of them properly. My partner thinks we should consolidate them. I don't even know what 'consolidate' means in this context. We have one kid and a small mortgage.
expected_llm_claims: Auto-enrolment workplace pensions are the default UK retirement vehicle for employees.
You should transfer your old Aviva pension into your current workplace scheme this month.
Consolidating pensions can simplify administration but sometimes loses valuable guarantees.
It's guaranteed to grow your retirement savings.
